text.p: Abraxas Petroleum Corp expects daily production to rise to 17,000 barrels of energy equivalent per day from 14,900 at the end of the first quarter, the company's chief financial officer told a conference call after first quarter earnings.
"I would say that 17,000 barrels is conservative," chief financial officer Chris Williford told the conference call.
He noted that the company was currently producing 15,600 barrels of energy equivalent.

The company said that 66 of its 106 wells to be drilled this year "could add incremental reserves to our reserve base" and said that its first quarter earnings of $0.28 a share were ahead of its own forecasts and way ahead of Wall Street analysts.
Analysts had been looking for a loss of $0.02 per share for the first quarter.

The company has traditionally relied on acquisitions to improve financial performance and said it had $19 million in cash on hand and a $40 million credit, which would allow it to pursue acquisitions.
The company has based its projections on $19.92 per barrel of oil and $2.25 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Abraxas said that it has some 75 percent of its oil output hedged for the rest of the year and more than 30 percent of its natural gas output. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
